captions.detailed: This 3D model depicts an exploded view of a customizable rectangular electronic enclosure. It consists of six flat panels (top, bottom, front, back, left, and right) designed to slot together. The edges of the panels feature fine interlocking ridges, resembling a brick-like or ribbed texture, to facilitate secure assembly. The top panel is slightly elevated in this view, demonstrating how the pieces fit together to form a protective box.
captions.instruction: Design a customizable, modular electronic enclosure in OpenSCAD. The script should allow users to define the device dimensions (width, length, overall height, and bottom height) and the wall thickness, with options to generate individual panels (top, bottom, left, right, front, back) or view them assembled in open or closed configurations.
captions.factory: The script defines several modular panels (top, bottom, side, front, back) by utilizing the cube primitive and combining them with boolean operations. Linear dimensions are parameterized using variables like device_width, device_length, and device_height. Small interlocking ridges on the joining edges are generated using iterative loops (for-loops) to create a series of small cylinders or cubes, which are then unioned or differenced to form the interlocking joints.
